ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=12$, $BC=5$. A square $CDEF$ is cut out from the triangle. What is the length of the side of square $CDEF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral CDEF is a square, \\
it follows that EF $\parallel$ CD, and EF = FC = CD = DE. Let EF = x, then AF = 12 - x, \\
therefore, $\triangle$ AFE $\sim$ $\triangle$ ACB, \\
thus, $\frac{EF}{BC} = \frac{AF}{AC}$, \\
which leads to $\frac{x}{5} = \frac{12 - x}{12}$, \\
solving this gives x = $\boxed{\frac{60}{17}}$, \\
meaning the side length of square CDEF is $\frac{60}{17}$.
